l.i: cipes detortum Similitudinem ab ipso Nazianzeno

main_text.l: SImilitudinem hanc Carnis & Spiritus semel in libris de
Pontifice obijcis; rursus repetis in Torto; in Responso ad
Apologiam inculcas denuò; post contra Barclaium ingeris;
atq; etiam insuper eam Lectori obtrudis in Epistola ad Anonymum:
quam crambeh quinquies iam recoctam in hoc
de Principum officio Tractatu reponis; ac si omnes fortunæ
vestræ, & totius Causæ vestræ ædificiū hoc potissimum
fundamento niteretur. Dabis (uti spero) mihi veniā, quùm
sis in vrgenda hac Similitudine impendio prolixior atque
impor tunior, si ego in ea refellenda maiorem operam insumam.
Greg. Nazianzenus spiritualem quidem Sacerdotū pote-
statem supra Principum anthoritatem, in merè spirituali-
bus, hòn minūs quàm spiritum carni (nec sanè imeritò)
præferendam esse iudicauit. At Principes, quoad externam
dignitatem, aut temporalem coercionem potestati Eccle-
siasticæ neutiquam subiecit: tantum enim abest vt Gregorius,
cognomento Theologus, tàm tetram [illegible, ~8 letters] Chri-
stianis propinaret, vt planè contrariam illi mentem fuisse,
vel mores ipsius demonstrent.

page.notes: Doubtful or illegible: "crambeh" (printed form uncertain, possibly crambem); "impor tunior" printed with a gap at the line end, read as one word; the Greek after "Princeps Philosophorum" and the Greek word after "tetram" are too faint to read letter by letter; the Greek word after "tetram" may be a form of Iudaismum, not confirmed. Show-through text from the reverse side behind "quod voluisti somniasti" and the summary line was left out. The mark in the left margin beside "Greg. Nazianzenus" is an ornament, not text. The initial S of "Similitudinem" is a drop cap, joined as "SImilitudinem". Marginal note "Sect.VII." placed beside the summary line.
